ai.description: *Lycodon gracilis* is a slender snake reaching 40–50 cm. It is brown with narrow, white, paired crossbands and a distinct white collar. It features a flattened head and a divided anal plate.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Lycodon gracilis* is best distinguished by its single preocular scale, which is in direct contact with the frontal scale, a feature absent in most other similar wolf snakes.
ai.habitat: *Lycodon gracilis* inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations up to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Scarce Bridal Snake is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively forage for small lizards and their eggs among leaf litter and rocky crevices.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon gracilis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon gracilis* occurs across the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Western Ghats, the Deccan Plateau, and parts of the Eastern Ghats, reaching elevations up to 1,000m.
